summary: ACCEPT. The approved Pass 1 Job Identity amendment is feasible, bounded, and closes the historical-job gap without weakening the iteration-6 runtime-binding contract. Newly dispatched ordinary Pass 1 packets use the actual server-derived Worker JobId over exactly ScanExecutionId, ScanRunId, RepositoryId, CodeUnitId, and the canonical full Profiled Revision; the sequential runner derives it immediately before dispatch, while the prepared-flow planner independently reconstructs the same current boundary and requires the existing CreateStableId("pass1-document-version", jobId.ToString("D")) Document Version projection before accepting the member. The version-1 domain-separated TLV contract is closed and cross-platform: distinct ASCII magic, fixed increasing tags and big-endian lengths, RFC-network-order UUID bytes, raw lowercase 40/64-hex Profiled Revision bytes, and UUIDv8-SHA256 projection are fully normative. Independent validation reproduced the specified 142-byte envelope, SHA-256 digest 6b9362f7193b38d94d9cb2a21ecfe2fd5ffe6a3aaaa00bd8c787e8efccdc71da, and UUID 6b9362f7-193b-88d9-8d9c-b2a21ecfe2fd exactly. The required repeat, per-input mutation, tuple/domain separation, collision/duplicate, legacy/random, substitution, projection-mismatch, drift, malformed, noncanonical, and mixed-endian tests make failure behavior observable before Pass 2 dispatch or persistence. Compatibility is explicitly fail-closed: existing random-ID Documents are neither migrated nor backfilled, the final accepted run begins from a clean database, and deterministic identity does not add retry scheduling, duplicate-dispatch permission, commit idempotency, concurrency, failover, clustering, or general Scan behavior.
